events.excerpt: Hello Phoenix Labs, BA Labs and Spark contributors, We would like feedback on a small Spark Liquidity Layer pilot with Zyfai , on Ethereum mainnet only, before any formal proposal. TL;DR Zyfai would run up to 10M USDC from the SLL, rebalanced daily across USDC lending venues on Ethereum, including Spark Blue Chip USDC. Two risk tiers, chosen by Spark. Over the last 90 days, net of a 5% Zyfai fee, Spark’s margin over the Sky Savings Rate would have been: conservative: 96 bps, 1.7x Spark Blue Chip USDC (57 bps) aggressive: 278 bps, 4.9x Spark Blue Chip USDC On 10M per year: about $96k (conservative) or $278k (aggressive), against about $57k from Spark Blue Chip USDC. Spark keeps custody: the Safe is owned by SPARK_PROXY . Zyfai can only move funds between allowlisted venues or back to the ALM Proxy. No controller change: inflow uses the existing transferAsset path with a 10M rate limit. 1. Why The SLL earns the difference between venue yield and the Sky Savings Rate (SSR). Spark Blue Chip USDC is today Spark’s direct USDC allocation on Morpho: about 19.6M, almost all from the ALM Proxy, in two markets (cbBTC 86% LLTV about 85%, wstETH 86% LLTV about 15%). It cannot take much more size without lowering its own rate. Zyfai adds diversification and daily rebalancing across the main US

events.excerpt: Hi Polkadot community, I’d like to open a discussion about how Treasury proposals are evaluated, particularly when assessments are presented as formal technical or systemic risk audits. Our recent proposal, Referendum #1956 — ComputeFlux Pilot , received a comment titled “SYSTEMIC RISK AUDIT REPORT,” recommending a hard NAY vote. We fully respect everyone’s right to question Treasury spending, challenge proposals, and vote according to their own judgment. However, several claims in this assessment appear to overlook important facts about ComputeFlux, including our open-source infrastructure, Polkadot PVM smart contracts, existing product, and commercial business model. Rather than simply responding to one assessment, we’d like to raise a broader discussion about transparency, technical accuracy, and how the ecosystem evaluates teams that are actively building. 1. Who Is Behind These Treasury Audit Reports? We would genuinely like to understand: Who authors or operates these assessments? Are they affiliated with an established Treasury evaluation organization, or are they independent community reviewers? What technical methodology is used? Do reviewers examine publicly available source code and deployed infrastructure before issuing technical conclusions? Is there a process for co

events.excerpt: CODE_COLOR: CODE_YELLOW_MAINNET RELEASE_VERSION: 2.14.0 PROTOCOL_UPGRADE: TRUE DATABASE_UPGRADE: TRUE SECURITY_UPGRADE: FALSE Protocol Changes Remove gas rewards: executing a FunctionCall no longer pays part of the burned gas back to the contract account as a reward. The burnt_gas_reward parameter is changed from 30% (3/10) to 0%. See HSP-027 Added an ml_dsa_verify host function so contracts can verify FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signatures on-chain. It takes the signature (3309 bytes), an arbitrary-length message, and the raw 1952-byte public key, each passed either from memory or from a register, and returns 1 for a valid signature or 0 for an invalid one; a wrongly-sized signature or public key aborts the call with MlDsaVerifyInvalidInput . The message is verified as-is with an empty context string, so callers must not pre-hash it. It costs a fixed base cost of 540 Ggas and a dynamic per-byte cost of 11 Mgas per byte. The per-receipt storage proof limit now applies to every action in a receipt, not just FunctionCall . The recorded proof is checked after each action, and a receipt that goes over per_receipt_storage_proof_size_limit (4 MB) fails at that action with the new ReceiptStorageProofSizeExceeded error; the actions after it do not run. events.excerpt: Hi everyone, I’m Maxim from Timeus Lab, the team behind Atomic Launchpad. We’re deploying it to Arbitrum One this week, and before we do, we’d like to introduce it here and hear from delegates. What it is Atomic Launchpad lets anyone launch a token for 0.0005 ETH. Tokens trade on a bonding curve. When the curve fills, it graduates into its own Uniswap v4 pool, and the liquidity position is locked permanently. Two things set it apart: A graduation bar that starts low. For the first 72 hours after deployment, a token graduates at 0.01 ETH raised. After that, the bar rises every 4 hours, up to 4.2 ETH by day 30. Early creators get the cheapest path to a real pool. Creators earn on every trade. Each trade pays a 1% base fee, and a creator can add up to 10% on top, fixed at launch. Creators keep 70% of the fee, and the protocol keeps 30%. Why Arbitrum One DefiLlama lists 11 launchpads on Arbitrum. Together they earned less than $2 in fees over the last 30 days ( DefiLlama , checked October 26). A creator who wants to launch a token on Arbitrum One today has no live place to do it, so they launch on other chains and take their communities with them. Timing relative to the October 2 Security Council action The report was completed before the Security Council’s emergency action on October 2 , which temporarily paused activation of new Stylus contracts on Arbitrum One and Nova. The Council took the action as a precaution after AI-assisted tooling led to a rise in attacks using hand-crafted WASM programs built outside the standard Stylus toolchain. Known Stylus bugs affected chain liveness and did not put user funds at risk. Already-active Stylus contracts continue to run and can be renewed, and EVM contracts are unaffected. This proposal authorizes a new Stylus Activation Contract and delegates to the Arbitrum Foundation the right to authorize the activation of Stylus contracts that have passed a limited security audit performed by an Arbitrum Security Program auditor (explained in further detail below) and that focuses on whether the code threatens the stability (and security) of the Arbitrum network. The ArbitrumDAO can change or revoke this delegation via a constitutional vote at any time. Importantly, all existing and activated Stylus smart contracts are not impacted by this proposal or the Security Council action. Any user or developer can continue to use these contracts without restriction, and anyone can continue to renew them through the existing keepalive mechanism. Reactivation of an expired contract, or after a Stylus version change, follows the process in Section 4. events.excerpt: The Arbitrum Developer Guild was first introduced in January 2024 alongside the Arbitrum Expansion Program. We have published the first version of the Guild’s specification and it is available in the Arbitrum Foundation’s documentation. The Guild is an invite-only and merit-based program facilitated by the Arbitrum Foundation. Membership is assessed based on demonstrated proof of work on the core Arbitrum Protocol or other high-impact technical contributions to the ecosystem. Members must also demonstrate strong alignment with Arbitrum such that their company’s success substantially depends on Arbitrum winning. The Guild is currently funded through 2% of Net Protocol Revenue from Arbitrum Chains alongside 3% of the Priority Gas Auctions (PGA) and the Sequencer Fast Feed proceeds from Arbitrum One. There are more than 30 Arbitrum Chains who are already contributing to the Guild. Each member will receive an allocated percentage of the funding on a regular cadence. This funding is intended primarily as an additional incentive on top of the member’s core business revenue. With this framework now in place, we are pleased to announce the first member of the Arbitrum Guild: Offchain. events.excerpt: Russia's central bank is rapidly widening the list of firms allowed to trade crypto, as the country's two biggest lenders prepare to sell Bitcoin and other coins to ordinary customers before the end of the year. The Bank of Russia added a 17th company, Prosto LLC, to its register of crypto exchange providers on Thursday, according to a notice on the regulator's website . The register had four members when it opened on 6 October. The separate register of digital depositories, which record who owns which coins, now has eight. The registrations put into practice a law "On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights", which took effect on 1 September and brings crypto trading inside Russia's regulated financial system for the first time. Sberbank and VTB hold both licences Sberbank and VTB, Russia's largest state-controlled banks, were among the first five digital depositories approved on 6 October, the central bank said . VTB was also listed as a crypto exchange provider that day. Sberbank joined the exchange register on 12 October, Interfax reported . Holding both statuses lets a bank buy and sell crypto in its own name and keep the record of clients' holdings. Exchange providers can trade digital currencies for their own account outside organised venues, while depositories record and tr

events.excerpt: Proposal Type: Ratification Documents ratified: Operating Manual v2.1.0 Security Council Charter v0.2 Security Council Member Selection Criteria v0.1 Executive Summary The Optimism Foundation is proposing to ratify Operating Manual v2.1.0, Security Council Charter v0.2 and the Security Council Member Selection Criteria v0.1, which change how Security Council membership is determined. The Token House elects the Security Council Lead. The Lead may be removed at any time via a “Representative Removal” proposal. The Lead recruits, interviews and nominates the Council’s participants against the public selection criteria that are ratified by governance and the Security Council Member Selection Criteria. Nominees must clear Foundation KYC/KYB screening first. Each nominee is confirmed through a new proposal type, “Council Appointment”. A nominee is seated unless 20% of active votable OP supply vetoes that nominee. Each nominee is a separate proposal. Elections for Security Council cohorts are discontinued. The Operating Manual update also shortens the review period for proposals to one week, in line with current practice, and makes minor cleanup improvements. Motivation Current process: The Security Council runs three elections per year (Cohort A, Cohort B and the Lead), each by approva

events.excerpt: Towards Mainnet Interop: Introducing the Inaugural Unichain and OP Mainnet set proposal type: informational / discussion Summary We, Optimism Foundation and Uniswap Labs are preparing to launch native OP Stack Interoperability on Mainnet with an inaugural set consisting of Unichain and OP Mainnet . Subject to final technical readiness and governance approval, the two chains will be upgraded into a common Interop set. This will allow transactions on one participating chain to consume and validate messages initiated on another participating chain at the protocol level, without relying on a separate third-party bridge validator set. The first release will focus on native ETH transfers between Unichain and OP Mainnet . Broader token support, application-level integrations, and the addition of further chains will follow after the initial system has been deployed and proven in production. This post is intended to: Communicate the proposed inaugural chain set; Explain why Unichain is a go-to-market strong partner; Clarify what is and is not included in the initial release; Explain the relationship between upgrade 20, 21 and the subsequent Interop activation upgrade; and Invite governance feedback before the executable activation proposal is submitted. What Interop Changes Today, OP Stac

events.excerpt: Hi everyone, We just opened the public testnet of Luggom, a Cosmos SDK app-chain with one job: turn a real tax payment into money you own, proven end to end with TLSNotary. No KYC. No third parties. The bank session never leaves the user's device. ## Why another chain? Because Cosmos is at its best when an app-chain brings a new kind of user. Luggom brings the taxpayer. There is no subsidy and no token sale. The inflow is a real payment that already leaves people's accounts every year. The chain's job is to prove it happened and mint against it. ## How it works 1. The user pays a real tax at their bank, as always. 2. TLSNotary proves the paid receipt without exposing the session. 3. The notary signs the attestation; the chain verifies it and mints. 4. Each receipt mines exactly once (payment_id + proof_commitment anti-replay). The desktop app (Tauri/Rust) builds the proof request and signs locally. The seed never leaves the device. What is live - chain-id: `luggom-test` - RPC: `https://rpc.luggom.com` - LCD: `https://lcd.luggom.com` - API: `https://api.luggom.com` - Notary: `wss://notary.luggom.com/session` - Full nodes: open (p2p 26656) — seed `1530baa7b3a07e0cab8dc81c9c08fccc51a47471@62.146.183.122:26656` - Validators: by invitation (the operator funds 200 testnet LUG) - App +
events.headline: Luggom — a Cosmos SDK app-chain where you mine LUG by paying real taxes (public testnet)

events.excerpt: Opening community discussion on URC-5: Token Venue Policy . Some tokens recommend particular liquidity pools or restrict trading to supported venues, often because their mechanics depend on a Uniswap v4 hook (INDEX, STANDARD, FWA, etc). Without a shared way to discover those policies, routers and frontends need token-specific integrations and may otherwise offer unsupported routes. Anecdotally, STANDARD and FWA prevented a lot of trading volume due to routers routing to restricted pools and required bespoke integrations for both. URC-5 defines IVenuePolicy , a token-level interface for declaring canonical v4 pools, distinguishing Preferred and Enforced policies, and exposing directional permissions for other liquidity venues. It also specifies how routers, aggregators, and frontends should interpret those declarations. Transfer-time enforcement remains token-specific. We’d appreciate input from hook developers, token teams, routers, aggregators, and frontend implementers. 6 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
events.headline: URC-5: Token Venue Policy

events.excerpt: Reth v2.8.0 schedules the Amsterdam hardfork on Hoodi, adds opt-in snap/2 sync and prewarm result reuse, and hardens peer-to-peer networking and RPC. With the opt-in --engine.prewarm-reuse , reth commits prewarmed transaction results instead of re-executing them. This reduced mean latency by 12.35% and raised Mgas/s by 18.58% over 500 replayed blocks ( #27894 ). Per-block proof-worker sizing reduced mean execution time on 300M-gas BAL blocks by 8.41% ( #27196 ). RPC response compression no longer cuts throughput by up to 22x ( #27863 ). Action Required Hoodi operators must upgrade before 26 October 2026 at 17:42:48 UTC. This release schedules Amsterdam on Hoodi at timestamp 1793036568 (epoch 132352) and extends the Hoodi fork IDs through Amsterdam. ( Reth change , Hoodi schedule ) All operators should review the default and behavior changes under Breaking Changes, especially those affecting the gas price oracle, WebSocket origins and the minimum priority fee. Update Priority User Class Priority Payload Builders Medium Non-Payload Builders Medium Breaking Changes Runtime and Configuration Changed the default gas price oracle ignore threshold ( --gpo.ignoreprice ) from 0 to 2 wei to match Geth, so zero-tip transactions no longer pull eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas down to 0. Set --gpo.ig

events.excerpt: Summary The Cosmos Hub community pool holds 566,067.055810 USDC.n (Noble-issued USDC). Circle pauses the Noble USDC contract and all Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) routes to and from Noble on January 12, 2027. This proposal sends the full USDC.n balance of the community pool to a 4-of-6 DAODAO multisig composed of six Cosmos community members and validators to migrate to USDC.inj (Injective-issued USDC). The multisig will migrate the funds to USDC.inj and return the USDC.inj to the community pool. The multisig holds the funds for the duration of the migration only and has no other mandate. Changelog 2026-10-20: Draft posted for community discussion. 2026-10-21: Updated proposal with DAO address details and DAODAO links Background On September 10, 2026, Circle announced that it is discontinuing support for USDC and CCTP V1 on Noble as part of its transition to CCTP V2. Noble will not receive CCTP V2. The wind-down runs on the following schedule: October 13, 2026: New minting of USDC on Noble through Circle Mint is disabled. October 31, 2026: CCTP V1 burn limits from Noble begin reducing gradually to zero. January 12, 2027: The Noble USDC contract and all CCTP routes to and from Noble are paused. Circle snapshots remaining Noble USDC balances on this date. January 13, 2027: C

Update Arbitrum One and Nova L1-Pricing Parameters for Ethereum Glamsterdam Offchain proposes to prepare for Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade by updating the parentGasFloorPerToken and perBatchGasCharge parameters on Arbitrum One and Arbitrum Nova. Because Glamsterdam changes the Ethereum gas costs associated with posting Arbitrum chain batches, these parameter updates would ensure that the L1 fee paid by Arbitrum One and Nova users accurately reflects the cost of posting batches to Ethereum. Voting ends on October 22. 2. Establish an L1 Voting Recovery System Offchain proposes an L1 voting system that allows ArbitrumDAO proposals to be created, voted on, queued, and executed from Ethereum L1. This system wouldn’t replace normal L2 governance nor modify the Security Council’s authority, rather, it is intended as a last-resort recovery path if normal L2 governance is broken and the Security Council is unable to act. Voting ends on October 22. 3. Transfer 1,700 ETH from the Treasury to the Arbitrum Developer Guild & ATMC’s ETH Treasury Strategies Entropy proposes to transfer ~1,615 ETH accrued from Sequencer revenue to the ATMC; and ~86 ETH accrued from Timeboost and PGA revenue to the Arbitrum Developer Guild (ADG). events.excerpt: # [Discussion] Mirror Staking: Forcing Ecosystem Value Realignment via the “Slacker Tax” ## Summary The Cosmos Hub faces a persistent value-capture gap: external chains utilize our free, open-source software (Cosmos SDK/IBC) without accumulating the ATOM token. This proposal introduces a **Dual-Token Mirror Staking Model** designed to be adopted by consumer chains or app-chains. It rewards aligned validators with a premium yield tier funded entirely by taxing unaligned (“Slacker”) validators, creating a systemic, non-inflationary supply shock for ATOM. -– ## The Problem: The ATOM Yield Trap Current app-chain models rely heavily on hyper-inflation to sustain high staking yields. This dilutes the token price, trapping validators on a financial treadmill where fiat revenue drops despite high token APR. events.excerpt: Hey Cosmonauts, I’ve been exploring an idea for a privacy-focused Cosmos SDK chain and wanted to bring it here before going too far into implementation. The idea is called VeilRoute — a sovereign Cosmos blockchain that acts as a confidential settlement and asset-routing layer between IBC-connected chains. The problem I’m interested in is relatively simple: Cosmos has interoperability through IBC, but what if applications could route assets through a common privacy layer without publicly exposing every internal transfer, amount, balance, or ownership relationship? I’m not proposing changes to the Cosmos Hub or requesting governance funding. This is an early architectural discussion to get technical feedback from people working on Cosmos SDK, IBC, ZK systems, and interchain security. 1. The idea Imagine a user moving ATOM from Cosmos Hub to Osmosis. Today, the public source and destination transactions are observable, along with the relevant IBC packet information.
